messages:
Maria: FYI I ran the long-context replay after the kernel-selector tweak on canary and saw a clear regression for prefill-heavy traces. p95 up ~20%.

Akshay: which tweak exactly? the selector change from yesterday?

Maria: yes. I lowered the kernel_switch_slew threshold to make smaller kernels preferred. Config snippet I used:
```
kernel_selector:
  mode: adaptive
  slew_threshold: 0.22  # was 0.5
  prefer_cuda_amp: true
```

Dave: okay. I can believe that hurts big-prefill flows. Small kernels are great for short-turnaround requests but might cause more kernel churn when a single request has a long prefill.

Lena: we should compare apples-to-apples: replay trace vs synthetic must match prefill fraction and prefill length distribution and KV hit-rate. Our synthetic profile had too few long-prefill cases.

Maria: repro details: replay harness against customer-trace-2025-02-16 (prefill-heavy). KV-hit ~0.11. Baseline vs change:
- baseline (slew=0.5): p50=70ms p95=205ms tokens/s=12.1
- slew=0.22: p50=76ms p95=246ms tokens/s=9.6

perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/graphs/1863001234/flame-2025-02-16.svg. Profiler shows lots of time in select_kernel and increased memcpy around prefill->generate boundary.

Akshay: can you run the same replay but force fixed-kernel to see if adaptive is the culprit? we need same request ordering/seed.

Maria: running fixed now with seed=9123. Command: `./harness/replay --trace=customer-trace-2025-02-16 --seed=9123 --kv-hit=0.11 --seqlen-profile=long-prefill.json --force-fixed-kernel`

ci-bot: queued: run/bench-1863001234-fixed-vs-adaptive. Artifacts will land at https://ci.internal/1863001234/artifacts

Maria: quick local synthetic run with updated long-prefill mix I proposed: `--seqlen-dist mix:short=0.5,mid=0.3,long=0.2 --prefill-fraction=0.42 --prefill-mean=1350 --kv-hit=0.11` shows the same pattern.

Dave: hypothesis: adaptive selector overhead (select + kernel spin-up + potential KV rebind) isn't amortized when large prefill chunks cause multiple kernel switches. Two fixes to test: (1) minimum_stability_tokens (don't switch kernels until N tokens pass), (2) prefer single larger kernel on prefill-dominant path.

Lena: +1. Let's try minimum_stability_tokens=128 and measure: kernel_switch_count, kv_bind_ops, select_kernel latency. Also add an apples A/B benchmark that runs both modes against identical replay traces and seeds.

Maria: CI A/B results are in: fixed-kernel p95=218ms tokens/s=11.3; adaptive (slew=0.22) p95=244ms tokens/s=9.7. Fixed-kernel wins for this trace.

Akshay: rollback the canary change for now?

Maria: rolled back on canary hosts and opened PR to add stability window gated by a feature flag + benchmark config for long-prefill apples tests. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3728

Dave: please add a nightly replay that covers a corpus of long-prefill traces so we catch this class earlier. Also log kernel_switches_per_100k_tokens and kv_bind_ops_per_request as KPIs.

Lena: I'll add alert: kernel_switches_per_100k_tokens spike >20% triggers Slack alert to #eng-runtime.

perf-bot: scheduled: nightly-replay-long-prefill job/1863001234. Summary will post to artifacts.

Maria: action items recap:
- PR to add minimum_stability_tokens flag + revert on canary (Maria)
- Add apples-to-apples long-prefill synthetic config to bench suite (Dave)
- KPI + alert (Lena)
- Run extended replay corpus overnight and post consolidated metrics (Akshay)

Maria: trace and flamegraphs on NFS: /mnt/perf/traces/customer-trace-2025-02-16 and /mnt/perf/graphs/1863001234. Ping me if you want to pair on the flamegraphs.

Akshay: will check in 45m, thanks :thumbsup:
